title: Eventflow continuity negotiator and client grace policy for SSE streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: design and implement a lightweight continuity negotiator and client grace-window policy for Server-Sent Events (SSE) based streaming responses. This ticket focuses on ensuring consistent structured output and tool/function-call atomicity across transient disconnects while minimizing protocol churn for older clients.

Scope:
- Define a small, server-first negotiation header set to indicate supported minimal resume semantics and heuristic checkpointing (no binary checkpoints).
- Add a short-lived, server-provided 'grace window' that allows clients to reconnect and reattach to an in-flight logical stream without full rehydration of state.
- Implement 'fragment seals' that mark semantic boundaries for structured JSONL chunks and tool-call frames so replays do not duplicate side-effecting tool invocations.
- Provide an opt-in compatibility shim: servers advertise a legacy mode for clients that cannot honor fragment seals; in that mode the server falls back to idempotency tokens per tool call.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We prefer a soft, heuristic-driven approach rather than rigid per-token checkpoints to keep latency and CPU overhead low. This trades exact-at-most-once guarantees for pragmatic idempotency and operator-visible reparability.
- Fragment seals use a compact 8-byte integrity tag (not a full SHA) so clients can cheaply detect chunk boundaries without heavy CPU costs. This tag is not a security feature but a detection aid.
- Tool/function-call atomicity: when a fragment includes a tool invocation frame, the server will include an invocation-id plus an idempotency token. If the client reconnects and the server cannot confirm completion, the runtime will consult the idempotency token before re-executing the tool.

API and header proposals:
- X-RW-Stream-Proto: 2 (major protocol level)
- X-RW-Resume-Window: milliseconds (server-suggested grace period)
- X-RW-Fragment-Tag: base64-8 (attached to final event of a fragment)
- X-RW-Compat-Mode: legacy|sealed (for server-side fallback)

Success criteria:
- End-to-end integration tests that simulate client disconnects at JSON field boundaries, in the middle of function-call frames, and across long-running tool calls.
- 95th percentile reconnect reattach latency < 120ms when resuming within the advertised grace window (measured in CI).
- No duplicate tool side-effects in >99.9% of simulated reconnect cases when idempotency tokens are present.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement server-side negotiation and fragment-tag emit only (no client exposure).
2) Add runtime idempotency lookup for tool invocations. Test with synthetic workloads.
3) Add client SDK support and enable sealed mode by default for new clients.
4) Gradual enablement with telemetry and an operator-facing kill switch.

Open questions:
- How long should default resume windows be for different tiers (hosted vs dedicated)?
- Should fragment tags be optional for embeddings/compact outputs?
- Clarify audit log requirements for attempted replays of tool invocations.
